newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Apasco results seen unimpressive. [CORRECTED 18:59 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Apasco results seen unimpressive. [CORRECTED 18:59 GMT]

text.p: Mexican cement producer Apasco SA is expected to post unimpressive results in the first quarter, and analysts are not expecting any surprises.
According to a survey of seven industry analysts by Reuters, Apasco will report per share profits of 0.54 centavos compared with 1.24 pesos in the first quarter of 1996.
Revenues are seen falling to 883 million pesos from 960 million, while the operating margin is seen at 17 percent, compared with 28.6 percent a year before.

Weak results are "largely attributable to year-on-year volume decline and cost expansion as opposed to volatile prices, which have in fact increased slightly on a quarter-to- quarter basis," said Ben Uglow, an analyst with Robert Fleming.

He said the company could show a drop in sold tonnage in Mexico by five percent compared with the first quarter of last year. That forecast compares with an average forecasted fall of 0.9 percent in the Reuters survey.
Uglow also said he saw an increase in cost per tonne of about 20 percent.
"It will be a bad report, and it will be disappointing if volumes do not grow between one and 1.5 percent," said Peregrine Winfield, a cement industry analyst at Paribas Capital Markets in New York.
The average forecast predicted Apasco's average realized price during the quarter was $69 per tonne, similar to the level at the end of 1996 (corrects timeframe).

The company raised its prices about two percent during the quarter compared with inflation of about 5.6 percent, a difference which is likely to squeeze margins, Sobani Warner, at Bear Stearns in New York, wrote in a recent report. Despite the relatively weak report, analysts said it followed a bright 1996 for the company and did not signal a turnaround in its fortunes. They said the company should see better prices and volumes in the second quarter.
"It is reasonable to expect (that results will come out weak in Q1 97), but it doesn't mark any downward trend," said Christopher Hussey at Goldman Sachs in New York.
Some analysts said Apasco may have lost one or two percentage points of its market share during the quarter. It ended 1996 with a market share of 26 percent.
